name: Adhiratneswarar Temple, Thiruvadanai
deity: Shiva as Adhiratneswarar (Aadanainathar), with the goddess Snehavalli
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Pandya Nadu in the Ramanathapuram country, sung by Sambandar in the Tevaram (7th century)
summary: In the dry Ramanathapuram country, Shiva is worshipped as Adhiratneswarar at Thiruvadanai, whose very name recalls the son of Varuna, cursed to the shape of a goat-headed elephant and restored here.

sections.history: Thiruvadanai is a taluk town in Ramanathapuram district, about 45 km from Karaikudi by way of Devakottai, and its temple is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams, counted among the fourteen of Pandya Nadu. Thirugnana Sambandar sang its Lord in a pathigam preserved in the second Thirumurai of the Shaiva canon. The Lord is known by three names — Adhiratneswarar, Aadanainathar and Ajagajeswarar — the last two drawn, like the name of the town itself, from the story of the curse lifted here.
sections.architecture: A nine-tiered rajagopuram, said to rise about 130 feet and crowded with stucco figures, announces the temple across the flat land around it. Within, the sanctum of Adhiratneswarar and the separate shrine of the goddess Snehavalli stand in their enclosures, along with a shrine of Surya Chandikeswarar. The temple waters include the Surya Pushkarini and the Varuna and Vaaruni theerthams, named for the figures of its legend, and the sacred tree is the vilvam.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of Vaaruni, son of Varuna, the lord of the waters, who was cursed by a sage to take the body of an elephant with the head of a goat. He came to this place and worshipped Shiva, and was restored to his own form. From aadu, goat, and aanai, elephant, the place became Thiru-aadanai, and the Lord Ajagajeswarar. Tradition adds that Surya, the Sun, also worshipped the Lord here.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Shaiva year — monthly Pradosham, Maha Shivaratri, Arudra Darshanam and the Navaratri days of the goddess. Snehavalli is associated with Sukra, the planet Venus, and devotees come to her shrine for prayers linked to that planet. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thiruvadanai is an unhurried town, and its tall gopuram is visible from far across the open country. Worship Adhiratneswarar and the goddess Snehavalli, look out for the temple's waters named after Varuna and his son, and combine the visit with the other Pandya Nadu shrines of the Ramanathapuram and Sivaganga districts.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer corridors, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruvadanai is about 45 km from Karaikudi via Devakottai and roughly 55 km by road north of Ramanathapuram, with regular buses from both. Karaikudi and Ramanathapuram are the nearest major railway stations, and Madurai Airport the nearest airport.
